sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 8:4

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 8:4:1
items.html: Even the three first ones are not yet corrected: For nothing whatsoever remained in them of all the Mochin of Gadlut that they had received in Nekudim, but only what came out in them in their very emanation, by force of the coupling of the bottom Hey in the Nikvey Einayim, as explained in the previous part. Therefore they lack all the phases of Gadlut. And this is what he says, that even the GAR are not corrected.

items.sefariaRef: Ohr Penimi on Talmud Eser HaSefirot 8:4:2
items.html:
This raising of Mayin Nukvin took place above, in AB and SAG of AK: Meaning that there is no raising of MAN except from a lower one to its upper one by one degree, that is, from ZON to AVI, and from AVI to AA, and the like, but not to the one that is two degrees above it. And this is what he says: since the GAR too require correction, and they too need the raising of MAN, it is therefore necessary that the upper phase of the raising of MAN be the Rosh of SAG. For the MAN of the ZAT are corrected in the AVI of Nekudim, and the MAN of AVI in the Keter of Nekudim, and the MAN of Keter in the first Rosh of Nekudim, and the MAN of the first Rosh of Nekudim are corrected in the Rosh of SAG, meaning each lower one in its own upper one.
And although he says above that all the MAN together — both those of the ZAT of Nekudim and those from the GAR of Nekudim — rose to the GAR of Nekudim, being the seven records of the seven lights of the ZAT together with the posteriors of HB and Keter, the intention is not that they were all corrected there together, but only by way of the degree, as above: that each lower one raised the MAN of its upper one to the upper of the upper one, and the upper of the upper corrects them for the sake of the upper one. In such a way that each one selected a portion out of the whole of the MAN and raised it to its upper of the upper, as written further along, until they rose to the upper AB and SAG.
